title: add-invocation-horizon-sampler-and-token-cost-origins
author: Leah Martinez
description:
Context: Long-tail SLO noise and prefetched-token accounting have been recurring pain points for customer-facing observability. Root cause: (1) existing samplers capture only past spans and biased warm traces, making it hard to surface which future-prefetch decisions (eg. cache pre-warm or assistant tool calls) actually drove cost spikes, and (2) token cost attribution treats all generated tokens as a monolith and loses origin semantics (system vs user vs prefetch vs tool).

Proposal: Introduce the Invocation Horizon Sampler (IHS) + Token Cost Origins mapper. IHS gathers an invocation-centric micro-window spanning pre-invoke signals, request lifetime, and a short "horizon" of downstream prefetch/tool invocations (up to 2s after invocation start) and emits a single sampled digest. The Token Cost Origins mapper annotates per-token cost/latency with an origin tag and phase (prompt, generation, tool, postprocess) so dashboards and alerts can attribute SLO noise to the correct causal surface.

What this PR changes: single-continuous description of changes and rationale. 1) Telemetry: add horizon-sampled invocation digest event, new schema fields: horizon_id, origin_tags, phase_breakdown, cost_signature. 2) Sampler: implement IHS in observability-sidecar with an adaptive sampling budget that prefers low-cardinality route+model pairs and keeps reservoir per-tenant. 3) Token attribution: enrich token emission pipeline to attach origin metadata pulled from the request graph (caller, tool, prefetch module). 4) Dashboard: add "Origin Cost Explorer" dashboard and an "Horizon Spike Investigator" panel that correlates horizon samples with kernel/backpressure metrics. 5) Alerts/playbook: add tuned alert rules that can suppress noise when origin is prefetch and route low-traffic. 6) Docs: add an observability-runbook section describing how to interpret origin tags and an example incident triage flow.

Motivation and tradeoffs: This approach increases event cardinality modestly but improves signal-to-noise for SLO debugging and cost RCA. The horizon window is conservative (2s default) to avoid unbounded correlation. We intentionally keep origin tags coarse (system/user/tool/prefetch/unknown) to prevent cardinality explosion.

Backward compatibility: New fields are additive; older consumers ignore horizon_id and origin_tags. Default sampling rate is off for free-tier tenants and enabled in staged rollout for prod tenants.

Rollout plan: staged in three waves: canary (internal + dev tenants), limited prod (5% traffic routed), wide (config to all). Monitoring: added dashboards and a synthetic probe (observability/ci job) to validate horizon sample capture.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation: sampler + token mapper + ingest schema
- [x] Unit/integration tests for horizon sampler and mapper
- [x] End-to-end synthetic replay test to ensure deterministic attribution
- [x] Docs + runbook update
- [x] Dashboard panels and alert rules added

Notes: Related to ENG-4521 (reduce SLO noise) and OBS-110 (prefetch accounting). This PR purposely avoids adding high-cardinality free-text origin labels; we can expand origin taxonomy in a follow-up after measuring cardinality.

release_notes: Introduce Invocation Horizon Sampler and Token Cost Origins: improves observability for prefetch/tool noise and enables origin-aware cost attribution. Add new dashboard 'Origin Cost Explorer' and 'Horizon Spike Investigator'. Alerts include origin-aware suppression toggles.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash on 2026-02-28 after approvals from Arjun, Maya, and Tomás. CI green. Patch was rolled out to canary tenants immediately and to 5% production traffic as part of staged rollout.
